AMD's Data Center segment net revenue for the quarter ended June 27, 2026 was $6.7 billion. This represents an increase of 107% compared to the prior year period, when the Data Center segment net revenue was $3.2 billion.
AMD paid $4.4 billion for ZT Systems. AMD received $2.4 billion in cash and 1.2 million shares of Sanmina common stock for selling ZT's manufacturing business.

AMD recorded approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges on AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products in the second quarter of fiscal year 2025. AMD reversed approximately $360 million of the inventory and related charges recorded earlier in the year during the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.
Applied Materials' days sales outstanding at July 26, 2026 were 77 days.

Applied Materials expected approximately 4% of its global workforce to be impacted by the Fiscal 2025 Restructuring Plan. The charges recognized under the Fiscal 2025 Restructuring Plan were $181 million, consisting primarily of severance and other employment termination benefits to be paid in cash, and other non-cash related charges.

Intel recognized a $12.5 billion loss related to the net change in the fair value of shares of its common stock released from escrow during Q2 2026. The fair value of the related derivative liability was $15.6 billion at the end of Q2 2026.
Broadcom's AI XPV platform initial tranche is $35 billion.
AWS sales grew by 37% in Q2 2026.
Alphabet raised $49.6 billion from its June 2026 equity issuances.

NVIDIA's most recent 10-Q describes the risk that its guarantees with SB Energy may expose it to substantial obligations over extended periods. The risk includes the possibility that SB Energy may not complete or deliver the infrastructure as expected or on schedule, which may delay or reduce anticipated benefits. If OpenAI does not perform its obligations or becomes subject to an insolvency event, and a guarantee is triggered, NVIDIA may assume the applicable lease, require the landlord to seek a replacement tenant, initiate a sale process or choose to pursue other remedies. A replacement tenant or buyer may not be found on acceptable terms or timing, any replacement lease or sale may generate less value than anticipated, and NVIDIA's obligations may continue longer than expected. NVIDIA may assume long-term lease obligations, incur ongoing lease-related costs or make substantial payments. Although OpenAI has agreed to reimburse and indemnify NVIDIA for certain losses, NVIDIA may not recover amounts promptly or in full.

If AI clouds cannot sell committed capacity, NVIDIA has agreed to purchase that capacity. NVIDIA may not have sufficient demand for, or the operational ability to use or resell, all the capacity it is committed to purchase. NVIDIA may earn a share of revenue generated by sales of the supported capacity, but lower-than-expected AI compute demand or pricing may reduce the revenue NVIDIA receives.

Microsoft's fiscal 2026 10-K identifies the availability, reliability, and cost of electrical power as critical to the operation and expansion of its datacenters. The 10-K states that limitations in power availability, delays in obtaining power connections, outages, shortages, increased energy costs, or requirements imposed by utilities, regulators, or other market participants could restrict Microsoft's ability to develop or expand datacenter capacity. The filing also mentions that alternative energy sources and other emerging solutions may not be available in sufficient quantities, may not timely scale to meet Microsoft's requirements, or may be available only at higher costs. If Microsoft is unable to secure adequate power resources on commercially reasonable terms, its ability to support customer demand and execute its growth strategy could be adversely affected.
Micron's latest 10-K does list customer concentration as a risk factor. The risk factor mentions dependency on certain customers, including international customers, and end markets.

Micron's fiscal 2025 10-K cites the decision by China’s Cyberspace Administration (the “CAC”) to restrict the purchase of Micron products by critical information infrastructure operators in China as a regulatory action affecting its business.

AMD relies on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (TSMC) for the production of all wafers for microprocessor and GPU products at 7 nanometer (nm) or smaller nodes. AMD relies primarily on GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. (GF) for wafers for microprocessor and GPU products manufactured at process nodes larger than 7 nm. AMD also utilizes TSMC, United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC) and Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. for our integrated circuits (IC) in the form of programmable logic devices.

AMD's fiscal 2025 10-K identifies that guarantees and commercial commitments supporting customers' infrastructure may increase exposure to counterparty risk, such as their inability to secure the necessary capital or financing, delays in project execution and downturns in their business, including insolvency. If AMD is required to satisfy its financial obligations under these commercial arrangements, its business, operating results, financial and condition may be adversely affected.

Applied Materials' customers are geographically concentrated, particularly in China, Taiwan and Korea, according to the risk factors in its most recent 10-Q.
According to the most recent 10-Q risk factors, Broadcom's top five end customers accounted for approximately 50% of its net revenue for the three fiscal quarters ended August 2, 2026.

Alphabet's most recent 10-Q describes that additional issuances of its Class A stock or Class C stock under its ATM Program could dilute its existing stockholders or otherwise depress the market prices of its Class A stock and Class C stock. The ATM Program allows Alphabet to offer and sell up to $40 billion of shares of its Class A stock and Class C stock, which could have dilutive effects for its existing stockholders over time. The market prices of Alphabet's Class A stock or Class C stock are likely to be influenced by any sales under its ATM Program, which could result in a depression in the market price due to dilution.

Amazon's most recent 10-Q indicates that developments affecting China-based sellers and suppliers are a risk because these entities account for significant portions of Amazon's third-party seller services and advertising revenues, and China-based suppliers provide significant portions of its components and finished goods. Regulatory and trade restrictions, tariff policy changes and trade disputes, data protection and cybersecurity laws, economic factors, geopolitical events, security issues, or other factors negatively impacting China-based sellers and suppliers could adversely affect Amazon's operating results.
